Does not create, does not explode, and looks like the guy in the corner office at a mid-sized insurance firm. Will need an entire team setting screens just to get him one open look.
projection: Projection: specialist. Waived the first time someone runs at him.

report: Senior wing with the frame of a coat hanger and the strength of a damp napkin. Long, smooth and capable of big shooting nights, but he will be bullied off his spot by anyone who has eaten breakfast. Defense is promising on paper, though the paper weighs more than he does. Four years of college and still built like a sixth grader mid-growth spurt.
projection: Projection: end-of-bench wing. Very good at stretching before games.

report: Undersized, earthbound power forward who left school early despite lacking length, lift, and a reliable way to score over taller people. Productive in college, but so was the team's student manager. Beefy and fundamentally sound, he is the kind of big who will spend his career getting his shot blocked by guys who were not even trying very hard.
projection: Projection: backup four. Fine rebounder, nice suits, short contracts.

report: Bulky, ground-bound freshman forward who plays below the rim, below the radar, and occasionally below sea level. Gets his rebounds by being wider than everyone else, which is not a skill that scales. Played limited minutes on a loaded roster and still left early, which is bold. Soft touch, nice footwork, but defensively he is a revolving door with no handle.
projection: Projection: offensive project. Needs a strict conditioning plan and stricter coaching.

report: Former high school phenom who spent one season coming off the bench and somehow dozed off in everyone's rankings. Elite explosiveness, a motor that should come with a warranty, and he throws his body around like it is a rental. The jumper needs work, but the effort is a full-time job by itself. This is the kind of athlete teams draft and then pretend they always knew.
projection: Projection: high-flying starter. Takes charges like he enjoys the paperwork.

report: Teenage point guard from an overseas pro league who weighs roughly as much as a carry-on bag. Lightning in the open floor, but the jumper is an unsolved case and the defense is a polite suggestion. Any legitimately physical workout partner will fold him like a lawn chair. Speed is nice; strength is mandatory, and he has not met it yet.
projection: Projection: two-year project, then back overseas running a club team.

report: Undersized scoring guard who is not a point guard, not quite tall enough to be a shooting guard, and somehow confident enough to be both. Shot selection is best described as interpretive. Fast, aggressive, and loves the ball the way some people love their phones. Teams will call him a tweener, and then they will call the next name.
projection: Projection: second-round scorer. Shoots his way off a roster by December.

report: Lanky, slow-footed overseas forward who looks like a math teacher who wandered into an open run. Can handle, can pass, has some size, but his defense is a sequence of polite waves at players going past him. The frame is narrow, the foot speed is glacial, and the jumper has more release points than a mixtape. Classic draft-night mystery box.
projection: Projection: three years on the bench, then a lengthy overseas encore.

report: Lefty scorer leaving school early after three seasons of firing away, with three-point percentages that made everyone in the building nervous. Strong frame and can get buckets inside, but the jumper is erratic and the defense is an afterthought he never got around to. A wing who cannot shoot is a scout's worst nightmare, and this one shoots constantly.
projection: Projection: deep bench. Garbage-time chucker with a long memory.

report: Went from bench piece to the guy running every late-clock possession in a single offseason, a growth curve that should frighten the league. Long, wiry wing who defends like he has a personal grudge against the opposing scorer. The jumper has a few moving parts, but the release looked better every week, and players who improve this fast do not stop. Carried a deep tournament run without breaking a sweat.
projection: Projection: franchise wing. Already measuring the rafters for his banner.

report: Plays with the unhurried calm of a man who has been doing this against grown professionals since middle school. Not a burner, and his vertical will not make the highlight reel, but he gets to every spot he wants by simply deciding to. Sees passing lanes before they exist and manipulates defenders like a chess hustler in the park. Has the size of a forward and the vision of a point guard.
projection: Projection: perennial MVP candidate. Will also lobby officials at an elite level.

report: Smooth combo guard who scores at all three levels with a jumper so pure it should be preserved in a museum. Changes speeds like a sports car with a perfect clutch, then finishes with either hand. Put up gaudy numbers on a losing team, which only proves he did it with zero help. The shooting stroke alone is worth the price of admission and will never, ever need adjustment.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard for fifteen years. The jumper is bulletproof.

report: Polished scorer with a footwork package that looks borrowed from a fifteen-year veteran. Lives in the midrange like he has a mortgage there and can get to his spot against any defender alive. Long, smooth, and still filling out, with a three-point stroke that kept improving as the season went. Some question whether he passes enough. Those people will be explaining themselves later.
projection: Projection: perennial All-NBA. Will win something big before the doubters log off.

report: Explosive wing who plays every possession like it owes him money. Elite athlete, relentless defender, and the kind of competitor who would dive for a loose ball in a pickup game. The jumper has a hitch, but he made strides all year and the work ethic suggests it gets fixed by Thanksgiving. Was the top-rated high school player in his class for a reason, and the reason is everything.
projection: Projection: two-way All-Star. Some will call him the best player in this draft.

report: Built like a light heavyweight and runs like one too, but basketball is unfortunately played with a ball. The jumper is a rumor, the handle is a dare, and the free throw shooting suggests the rim keeps moving on him. Spends a lot of time attacking the basket in a straight line, which works until the defense learns to stand there. Reportedly reads a lot. Concerning.
projection: Projection: athletic bench wing. Will dunk in warmups and little else.

report: Seven-footer who handles, passes, and shoots like a guard, which is the exact sentence every front office dreams of reading. Barely played for his pro club, but that only means the tape is all upside and no evidence. Slides his feet on the perimeter like a wing and is still a teenager, so the frame will fill out any minute now. The modern big man, arriving right on schedule.
projection: Projection: the mythical creature everyone else wishes they had drafted.

report: Seven-footer with soft hands, a feathery jumper, and post footwork that looks choreographed. Played limited minutes on a stacked roster, which hid nothing and revealed everything. Can face up, step out, protect the rim, and pass out of double teams like a guard trapped in a center's body. Young for the class and skilled beyond it, he is the rare big who checks every box on the form.
projection: Projection: perennial All-Star big man. Stretches the floor to the parking lot.

report: The most polished low-post scorer in years, which is a little like being the best fax machine repairman in the country. Has a drop step from a different decade and soft hands, but defends the pick and roll as if it were a rumor he once overheard. Rarely leaves the paint on either end. Free throws are an adventure the whole family can enjoy.
projection: Projection: big numbers on bad teams. Born roughly twenty years too late.

report: Athletic wing with a jumper that looks effortless and a confidence level that could power a small city. Played sparingly for one of the best clubs on his continent, which only means his coach was hiding a weapon. Explodes to the rim, shoots off movement, and carries himself like a guy who has already made three All-Star teams in his head. The personality alone sells tickets.
projection: Projection: high-flying All-Star scorer. He will tell you so personally.

report: The most NBA-ready scorer in the class, a forward who gets a bucket from anywhere using a bag of moves usually seen on thirty-year-olds. Strong, skilled, and equally comfortable facing up or backing down. Defense is a work in progress, but you do not draft a guy like this to stop people. Has been a household name since his early teens and has never once wilted under it.
projection: Projection: Rookie of the Year, then twenty-five a night for a decade.

report: Has played organized basketball for roughly as long as most prospects have been driving, and already moves like a ballet dancer stuffed into a seven-footer. Footwork is absurd, shot blocking is instinctive, and the touch says a jumper is coming. Back and foot issues are the one cloud in the sky, but you do not pass on talent this rare. Apparently learned post moves from watching tape on fast forward.
projection: Projection: franchise center and MVP candidate, assuming he can stay upright.

report: Mystery man with tape to match: grainy footage of a long, lightning-quick lead guard slicing through defenders who appear to be extras. Six-foot-six at the point with a first step that arrives before the defense hears it. Has not played college or high-level pro ball, so the jumper is theoretical and the upside is unlimited. Front offices describe him in terms usually reserved for sports cars.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard. The mystery is the best part.

report: A tweener in the purest sense: too small to bang inside, not quick enough to guard on the wing, and unable to work out for anyone thanks to a shoulder that needed surgery. Can score in bunches against mid-major size, which is a sentence doing heavy lifting. Defensive effort comes and goes like a bus schedule. Conditioning is listed as a work in progress.
projection: Projection: late lottery talent in a weak class. Someone will reach anyway.

report: Was a guard until a growth spurt turned him into a seven-footer who still handles and passes like one. Blocks shots like it is a personal hobby, runs the floor like a gazelle, and changes every possession on defense without leaving his spot. The frame is skinny and the offense raw, but those are the only two nitpicks, and both are temporary. Generational is an overused word. Not here.
projection: Projection: generational two-way big. Every team in the lottery is praying.

report: Bulldog scorer who came off the bench and still looked like the best guard on the floor. Built like a running back, gets into the paint at will, and has the swagger of a man who has never missed a shot in his own memory. Never started a game, which only proves he does not need the lights on to perform. Confidence is a skill, and he has the most in the building.
projection: Projection: star scoring guard. Will shoot his way out of any slump.

report: Relentless power forward with a body chiseled out of granite and a motor that never idles. Rebounds out of his area like the ball is personally addressed to him and finishes through contact with bad intentions. Was an afterthought one season and a national player of the year candidate the next. The jumper is still under construction, but you simply cannot teach this kind of energy.
projection: Projection: double-double machine for a decade. Will outwork the entire league.

report: Played only a handful of college games before a foot injury, and that handful was enough to make every front office reshuffle its board. Has a handle that seems illegal in at least three states, finishes off the glass with either hand from angles that should not exist, and shoots it with range. Small sample, enormous talent. Do not overthink this one.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard and a nightly highlight reel.

report: Seven-footer who runs the floor like a wing and dunks like he is trying to break the backboard as a personal statement. Athleticism at his size is rare anywhere and borderline unheard of on his league's grainy broadcast feeds. The shooting needs work, free throws especially, but you can teach a stroke. You cannot teach a seven-footer who plays above the rim like this.
projection: Projection: high-flying starter at the four. Highlight machine for years.

report: Fastest player with the ball in his hands in the entire sport, possibly in several sports. Gets coast to coast in about four dribbles and finishes with a flair that will sell season tickets on its own. The jumper is streaky and he turns it over, but that is what happens when your brain moves this fast. Plays like a guy who knows the cameras are following him, because they are.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard. Fastest man in the league on day one.

report: Long, smooth wing who can shoot it, defend multiple spots, and rise over the top for a dunk in traffic. Has an effortless stroke from deep and a physical maturity that makes him ready from the opening tip. Some will mention his age, but experience is a feature, not a bug. Projects as a plug-and-play starter who will be very good for a very long time.
projection: Projection: perennial starting wing. The safest pick in the top five.

report: Long-armed shot blocker who is already twenty-three, which in prospect years is roughly retirement age. Defends the rim with genuine instincts but treats the offensive end like a place he visits on weekends. Has one great season on his resume, much of it achieved against people years younger. Fine backup big. Drafting him in the top ten would certainly be a choice.
projection: Projection: rotation big who blocks shots and confuses the box score.

report: Throws down dunks with a violence that should require a permit. Freakish leaper for his size, explosive off one or two feet, and a monster on the glass who simply outjumps everyone in the zip code. The jumper is a rough draft and the free throws need work, but this is the most dominant college big in years. Has the motor of a sports car and the build of a moving van.
projection: Projection: franchise power forward. Will put somebody on a poster weekly.

report: Very tall. That is the report. Blocks shots because the ball keeps wandering into the space he occupies, but on offense he looks like a man assembling furniture without the instructions. Raw does not begin to cover it. The hands are unreliable, the footwork is still being installed, and he gets moved off his spot by smaller players who simply lean on him.
projection: Projection: tallest backup center in the league. Excellent at standing near the rim.

report: Plays below the rim and slower than he looks, which is saying something, because he looks slow. Lacks the explosion to beat elite athletes off the dribble and survives on change of pace and craftiness, tricks that tend to stop working against grown men. Defense is a philosophical question. A bulky lefty who might top out as a nice sixth man with a crafty floater.
projection: Projection: useful bench scorer. Nobody is building an offense around this.

report: Lightning-quick point guard with a motor that apparently runs on pure caffeine. Has the stamina to play an entire tournament weekend and look fresher at the end than the referees. Breaks down defenders in a phone booth, gets to the rim whenever he wants, and leads with the kind of fire you cannot teach. Small, sure, but every great little guard was small at some point.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard. Clearly the best guard in this draft.

report: A once-in-a-generation center who looks thirty-five and plays like he invented rim protection. Alters every shot within ten feet, owns the glass, and made a deep tournament run while shooting free throws with his off hand. Already has the strength of a veteran and the instincts of a Hall of Famer. Some prefer the skinny scorer. Those people do not understand winning.
projection: Projection: decade-long anchor of a champion. The obvious first pick.

report: Seven-foot wingspan, guard skills, and a jumper that goes in from any spot on the floor, including some spots that are not technically on the floor. Scored at a historic rate as a freshman and made it look like a casual pickup run. The frame is pencil thin and the weight room has not been kind, but nobody ever won a scoring title by lifting a car. A pure bucket.
projection: Projection: multiple scoring titles. The skinny kid will be just fine.

report: The adult in every room. Proven winner on the biggest stage who does every unglamorous thing right: sets bruising screens, makes the extra pass, and defends the pick and roll like he wrote the coverage. Not flashy, not loud, just relentlessly correct. Can step out and shoot it a little, and the feel suggests a lot more is coming. Will still be winning playoff games when his classmates are coaching.
projection: Projection: perennial All-Star big. Meaningful minutes well into his late thirties.

report: Seven-footer who runs like a deer and splashes jumpers from the elbow with a release that looks lifted from a guard. Dominated his pro league with athleticism you rarely see at his size. Footage is limited and private workouts were, let us say, selective, but the glimpses are breathtaking. A face-up big who could change how teams think about the four.
projection: Projection: All-Star stretch four. Mismatch nightmare from day one.

report: Long, mobile big with soft touch, a high release, and a turnaround jumper that is basically unguardable at his height. Runs the floor, protects the rim, and has a frame that will carry another twenty pounds of muscle without losing a step. Polished enough to play now and still nowhere near his ceiling. The kind of big man coaches happily build an offense around.
projection: Projection: multi-time All-Star. Will live on the left block for a decade.

report: Can score from anywhere against anyone, which is fortunate, because he will need to score twice as much as he gives up. Moves laterally like a filing cabinet, lacks the burst to separate from NBA wings, and defends with the urgency of a man waiting for a table. Elite shooter, elite competitor, and the athleticism of a guy who drives a minivan to the gym.
projection: Projection: college legend. Struggles mightily once everyone is an athlete.

report: Leaps like the court is a trampoline and blocks shots from angles that defy physics. Came out of nowhere to become the most explosive athlete in the entire draft, and he is still learning the game, which is terrifying for opponents. Raw offensively, sure, but you cannot teach a vertical like this. The upside is a perennial Defensive Player of the Year who dunks on your head.
projection: Projection: defensive monster and highlight machine. The potential is limitless.

report: Battle-tested four-year big who treats the paint like a place of business and rebounds as if every miss owes him back pay. Elite shot blocker, physical, mature, and ready to contribute from day one. Not the highest ceiling in the class, but the floor is a sturdy, dependable starter who does the dirty work for fifteen years. In a draft full of mysteries, he is a sure thing.
projection: Projection: reliable starting big for fifteen years. Zero chance he misses.

report: Built like a linebacker straight out of high school, with shoulders that look borrowed from a much older man. Runs, jumps, rebounds, and blocks shots with a blend of size and explosion that has scouts reaching for the thesaurus. The offensive game is raw and the post moves are mostly theoretical, but nobody this young has looked this physically ready. The smile alone could sell out an arena.
projection: Projection: franchise center and perennial Defensive Player of the Year.

report: The most scrutinized teenager the sport has ever produced, and somehow he has exceeded the coverage. Built like a grown man, sees the floor like a veteran point guard, and finishes through contact like a tight end. There is no weakness worth listing, and mentioning the jumper feels petty. Front offices have been tanking in their hearts for two years.
projection: Projection: all-time great. Possibly still playing when your kids get drafted.

report: Seven-footer with soft hands, a lefty touch, and the mobility of a wing, still a teenager and already battling grown pros. Every workout has scouts walking out in stunned silence. Not much game footage exists, but the glimpses suggest a modern big who can do everything. The rare prospect who would go first overall in any normal draft, and some think that sells him short.
projection: Projection: franchise big man. Teams will regret passing on him for years.

report: Led his team to a title as a freshman by scoring from every spot on the floor in every way available. Big, strong forward with a jab step that freezes defenders like they have been unplugged. Can post smaller wings, face up bigger forwards, and will shoot his team into or out of anything. The most NBA-ready scorer in the class. It is not close.
projection: Projection: perennial scoring champion. Will hold the ball and make it worth it.

report: Stands well over seven and a half feet with the touch of a guard, a soft jumper, and passing instincts that make no sense for a man who ducks through doorways. Has dominated his pro league for years and moves far better than a body this size has any right to. Strength needs work against NBA brutes, but the skill level is otherworldly. A matchup problem every single night.
projection: Projection: perennial All-Star center. Will need a custom everything.

report: Explosive lead guard with a championship on his resume and a national player of the year trophy on his shelf. Scores in bunches, pushes the pace, and carries a winner's poise that never wavers. Can get to the rim or pull up from deep, and already plays like a ten-year veteran. The safest bet in the lottery to become a star, no questions asked.
projection: Projection: franchise point guard. An All-Star within three seasons.

report: Seven-footer who can shoot from deep, handle in transition, and run the floor like a guard. Only a teenager and already getting minutes for a pro team in a serious league, the kind of experience that ages prospects in the best way. The stroke in workouts was so pure some scouts thought they were watching a wing. Pencil thin, sure, but the weight room fixes that.
